contracts.signal: Celestica revealed its 'digital native' customer is OpenAI: initial deliveries of custom racks commence later in 2026 (samples 2026), with the program ramping in 2027 and well into 2028. As strategic systems partner, Celestica collaborates with OpenAI and Broadcom on multi-generational custom accelerator roadmaps, beginning with the Jalapeno accelerator (mass production planned 2027), supporting multi-gigawatt scale deployments. Program expected to carry consignment dynamics — material cost will not flow through Celestica revenue.

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q1 FY2026: revenue $4.05B (+53% YoY), adjusted operating margin 8.0% (company record), adjusted EPS $2.16 (+80% YoY), adjusted GM 11.3%, ROIC ~50%. CCS segment $3.24B (+76%, 80% of revenue) — communications +69%, enterprise +101%; HPS (Hardware Platform Solutions) $1.7B (+63%). Raised FY2026 outlook: revenue $17B -> $19B (+53%), adjusted EPS $8.75 -> $10.15 (+68%), operating margin 8.1%, CCS ~70% growth. Q2 guide $4.15-4.45B.
quarterly_data.figure: $4.05B rev (+53%), EPS $2.16; FY26 raised to $19B / EPS $10.15

quarterly_data.signal: Multiple 800G Ethernet switch programs ramping across the largest hyperscaler customers (plus continued 400G); 1.6T switch programs beginning mass production in 2H 2026 with two hyperscaler customers — 10 active 1.6T programs ramping heavily into 2027. Landmark win: a 1.6T co-packaged-optics (CPO) Ethernet switch for a hyperscaler — believed to be the first major production-scale CPO deployment, integrating a Broadcom Tomahawk module directly into the system (mass production 2H 2027). Also a 'digital native' fully-integrated compute+networking rack-scale program entering production in 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: 800G ramping; 10 active 1.6T programs; 1.6T CPO (Broadcom Tomahawk) win, MP 2H2027

quarterly_data.signal: Switch production cadence: multiple 800G Ethernet switch programs ramping now; MASS PRODUCTION of 1.6T switch programs begins with TWO hyperscaler customers in H2 2026; the landmark 1.6T co-packaged-optics Ethernet switch win reaches mass production in 2027. Management's CPO view: each hyperscaler adopts on its own path — some choose CPX before CPO — and 'the major adoption will be at 3.2T'. Supply, not demand, is pacing growth (extended lead times on advanced components; demand 'durable and cumulative').
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T MP H2 2026 (2 hyperscalers); CPO MP 2027; major CPO adoption at 3.2T

quarterly_data.signal: Record Q2 FY2026: revenue $4.70B (+62% YoY), adjusted operating margin 8.2% (new company high), adjusted EPS $2.54 (+83%), adjusted GM 11.5%, ROIC ~55%. CCS $3.81B (+84%, 81% of revenue) — communications +62%, enterprise +167% (accelerated hyperscaler AI/ML compute ramp + storage); HPS $1.9B (+58%, 41% of revenue). FY2026 raised again: revenue $19B -> $20.5B (+65%), adjusted EPS $10.15 -> $11.30 (+87%), op margin 8.4%, FCF $600M. Q3 guide $5.25-5.55B (+69%). 2027 revenue growth rate expected to ACCELERATE past 2026's 65%, with EPS growth outpacing revenue.

Digital native customer revealed as OpenAI: initial custom-rack deliveries later in 2026, ramping 2027 well into 2028 — a multi-billion dollar revenue opportunity. Celestica is strategic systems partner collaborating with OpenAI and Broadcom on multi-generational custom accelerator roadmaps, starting with the Jalapeno accelerator (mass production 2027) toward multi-gigawatt scale deployments. OpenAI program expected to run with consignment dynamics (material cost not in revenue).
quarterly_data.figure: OpenAI Jalapeno racks: samples 2026, MP 2027; multi-billion $ opportunity

quarterly_data.signal: Networking cadence: 1.6T mass production ramps commence in Q3 2026 with two hyperscaler customers; 10 active 1.6T programs 'really surging' in 2027 with additional awards likely in coming quarters; 400G 'remarkably resilient' from 2026 into 2027 alongside strong 800G growth. The 1.6T CPO switch win: samples 1H 2027, mass production 2H 2027. Scale-up TAM expected to grow substantially over next 3 years; also winning scale-up networking programs from one of its largest customers.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T MP from Q3 2026; 10 active 1.6T programs; CPO samples 1H27, MP 2H27

quarterly_data.signal: Supply & capacity: demand exceeds the guided revenue figures — the constraint is material, not capacity (some component lead times well above 52 weeks); customers placed non-cancellable, non-refundable orders for long-lead silicon and Celestica holds supply agreements on memory and PWBs. Gaining share as customers shift dual-sourced programs back to Celestica for reliable at-scale execution. Capacity expansions in Thailand, Japan, Richardson TX and Fort Worth TX; ~2,000 design engineers by end of 2026. FY26 capex ~$1B, ~$1.5B placeholder for 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: demand > guided revenue; lead times >52 wks; capex $1B FY26 / ~$1.5B FY27

quarterly_data.signal: Memory-inflation demand destruction documented: AI data-center memory demand is squeezing supply and raising prices for handset OEMs — Chinese OEMs cut build plans and drew down channel inventory, leaving Qualcomm's China Android shipments 'meaningfully below end-consumer demand' for two straight quarters; China handset revenue expected to BOTTOM in fiscal Q3 and resume sequential growth after. QCT handset guided down to ~$4.9B on these dynamics.
quarterly_data.figure: China handset builds cut on memory prices; bottom expected fiscal Q3

quarterly_data.signal: FQ3 2026 (ended 06-28-2026): revenues $9.9B — at the HIGH END of guidance 'despite a challenging MEMORY AND SUPPLY environment' — with GAAP EPS $1.87 and non-GAAP EPS $2.21. The memory squeeze predicted last quarter materialized: HANDSET REVENUE $5,086M, DOWN 20% YoY. Diversification offset: combined QCT AUTOMOTIVE AND IoT revenues +28% YoY, with automotive posting its 23RD CONSECUTIVE QUARTER of double-digit growth. COST PASS-THROUGH CONFIRMED: 'the semiconductor industry is experiencing a BROAD-BASED INCREASE IN INPUT COSTS across wafer fabrication, assembly, test, advanced packaging, MEMORY and other materials. We are taking concrete actions to reflect the higher input costs in OUR PRODUCT PRICING' — expected to benefit gross margins over time. FQ4 guide: revenues $9.7-10.5B (QCT $8.4-9.0B, QTL $1.2-1.4B). Returned $2.3B to stockholders in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: FQ3 $9.9B (high end); handsets $5.09B DOWN 20% on memory costs; auto+IoT +28%; pricing actions

quarterly_data.signal: AI-stack move: COMPLETED THE ACQUISITION OF MODULAR INC, 'creating an open software foundation for GENERATIVE AND AGENTIC AI' — a software layer complementing Qualcomm's custom data-center silicon entry (first shipments to a leading hyperscaler expected later this calendar year, per last quarter) and its edge-AI franchise.
